gaps.sentence: Students ___ to buy the textbook; copies are available in the library.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' plus the infinitive expresses absence of obligation: don't have to buy.

gaps.sentence: Candidates ___ switch off their phones before the exam begins.
You ___ park here — the police tow cars away every morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' expresses a rule you must not break: mustn't park.

gaps.sentence: They ___ have checked the dates before booking — now they have lost the money.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' expresses criticism of something not done: should have.

gaps.sentence: It is the only blue house on the street, so you ___ miss it.
gaps.explanation: 'You can't miss it' is an idiom meaning it is impossible not to find: can't.

gaps.sentence: You ___ tell anyone about this — it is a secret.
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' makes it clear the action is not allowed: mustn't tell.

gaps.sentence: You really ___ to apologise before this gets worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses advice similar to 'should': ought to apologise.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better not be late again; the boss is getting tired of it.
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'had better' places 'not' after 'better': had better not be.
